messages.subject: alter legend colour
parts:
Dear all,


I have attached a graph where it is almost impossible to see the colour of the legend. For some reason there is a white mist over the colours which I'd prefer not to have. Also, how can I make the pink and turquoise lines of the legend more visible, e.g. how can I make the lines thicker?


I've also tried to find out how to change the colours of the bars but was unable to change the line and the fill at the same time. With e.g. “scale_colour_manual(values = c("#colour", "#colour")” I only managed to change the lines but not the fill. Can you please suggest me an approach for this problem as well?


This time I've attached the script, the dataset, and the PDF of the graph.


Many thanks and best wishes,


Martin

messages.subject: Re: alter legend colour
parts:
Hi:

I have to admit that I'm not a big fan of stacking, so I modified your plot call to place the crossbars side-by-side (using position_dodge) and included a call to scale_fill_manual() to do the alpha transparency. I think it's easier to read, but it's one person's opinion.  Here's my modified code:

df <- structure(list(trt = structure(c(2L, 1L, 2L, 1L), .Label = c("female",

ggplot(df, aes(fill = group, colour = group, y = resp, x = trt)) +
    geom_crossbar(limits, width = 0.5, position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
    opts(legend.position = c(0.77, 0.89), legend.background = theme_rect(colour = 0)) +
    opts(legend.text = theme_text(face = "italic", size = 17)) +
    opts(legend.title = theme_blank()) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = alpha(c('red', 'green'), 0.2)) +
    labs(x = "sex", y = "time to be replaced [h]\n") +
    opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(size = 15, vjust = 1),
             axis.text.y = theme_text(size = 15, hjust = 1)) +
    opts(axis.title.x = theme_text(size = 25, hjust = 0.535),
             axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 25, angle = 90, vjust = 0.67, hjust = 0.78))

The changes are in line 2 (adding a position = statement) and in line 6 (addition of scale_fill_manual()).

The scale_fill_manual() code should answer the questions about color choice and alpha transparency not leaking to the legend, but I couldn't figure out how to control the line thickness in the legend (a very good question, BTW). I'm interested in knowing how this works, too.

HTH,
Dennis
